body:
Water Quality Findings — draft for annual report

Draft prepared during the winter drafting round. Summary of citizen sampling across the 14 coalition sites. Phosphorus reported in mg/L against the 0.1 mg/L regulatory limit; PFAS in ng/L against the 4 ng/L EPA action level.

Headline: 12 of 14 sites below the 0.1 mg/L phosphorus limit, with two sites approaching. No site over the limit as of this draft.

  • Site 9 (Johnson Creek): 0.071 mg/L, below, watch.
  • Site 10 (Johnson Creek, Milwaukie confluence): 0.078 mg/L, approaching.
  • Site 12 (Fairview Creek, below CAFO parcel): 0.089 mg/L, approaching.
  • All other sites below limit.

PFAS: exceedances noted at Columbia Slough sites and Johnson Creek; final PFAS list to be confirmed against the fall pull. Numbers here are from the February sampling and need refresh before the section is finalized.
title: Water Quality Findings — draft (winter round)

body:
Annual Report — section outline

Assembly page for the Multnomah County Clean Water Coalition annual report. Target completion November 1 2026. Sections: Director's letter (Cortez), Water Quality Testing (Stuart), Advocacy and CAFO campaign, Finance summary, Volunteer program.

  • Water Quality Testing section owner: Stuart Myer.
  • Needs: trued-up 14-site findings, threshold count, PFAS classification, board brief for the October 22 2026 hearing.
title: Annual Report — section outline

body:
CAFO campaign — summary notes

Working notes for the CAFO permit opposition heard by the Multnomah County Board on October 22 2026. Core argument rests on phosphorus loading downstream of the ag parcels, especially the Fairview Creek site. Keep all raw data and strategy internal to the coalition board.

  • Lead site of concern: Fairview Creek, below the CAFO parcel.
  • Supporting: Johnson Creek trend.
  • Do not release externally before board approval.
title: CAFO campaign — summary notes

body:
PFAS tracking — program notes

PFAS sampling started this year across the 14 sites. Reported in ng/L against the 4 ng/L EPA action level. Keep units in ng/L; do not convert to µg/L in reporting. Fall pull is the current reference for the annual report.
title: PFAS tracking — program notes
